incident-bot: Pager fired for reserved-pool-saturation (tenant=Novus, pool=novus-reserved-1) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Alert details -> 95th latency > 1200ms, 5xx rate 18% over the last 5m, queue_length=312, backpressure=true
pagerduty: https://pagerduty.example/INC123456 triggered by metric-alert/reserved-pool-saturation
maya cox: acked on pagerduty :white_check_mark: I'm on it. starting triage.
ryan kim: oncall standby. maya if you need escalation ping me.
maya cox: quick health dump: avg tokens/sec per GPU down 40%, model workers OOMs spiked on 3 nodes. logs show frequent `EvictWorker` events.
ops-runner: copying log tail:
```
[2024-05-21T15:02:11Z] worker-7: KVCache overflow, spilling to disk
[2024-05-21T15:02:14Z] worker-2: alloc failed, OOM reserve 0.2
[2024-05-21T15:02:17Z] scheduler: request queue length=312, head_latency=1320ms
```
maya cox: customer Impact: Novus reports elevated error rates in production (they're seeing 502/504 on inference calls). Novus CS said their dashboards show ~30% failed requests since 15:00 UTC.
novus-cs: we got several support tickets. customers are seeing timeouts in the product. escalating to account team.
ryan kim: immediate mitigation options: 1) increase reserved pool capacity (if spare GPUs available), 2) enable overflow routing to shared-hosted for Novus traffic, 3) apply soft rate-limits at ingress for tenant to shed non-critical traffic.
sre-lead: check quota for spare GPUs in region us-west-2. If we can hot-attach, do that as quick win.
ops-runner: spare capacity looks limited. two idle GPUs in us-west-2 general pool. can attach but needs config update and model hot-load, ~7-9 min.
maya cox: I'm going to enable overflow routing for Novus to route 20% of requests to shared-hosted fallback (preserve tokens for critical routes). doing config change now.
incident-bot: routing policy update submitted: set tenant=Novus overflow_percent=20 -> pending rollout.
maya cox: rollout done, waiting 30s for metrics.
ryan kim: simultaneously raise reserved pool from 4->6 (request submitted to dedicated autoscaler). ops-runner is on that.
ops-runner: autoscaler accepted the request, creating 2 nodes, starting image pull. progress: node-9 provisioning -> 45%
maya cox: adding temporary ingress rate-limit for Novus non-prod keys (shave off tail). applying `rbac` rule now.
novus-cs: will notify Novus account team that mitigation in progress (overflow + capacity increase). They asked for ETA.
sre-lead: ETA rough: overflow change immediate; capacity + model warm-start ~10min; expect error rate to drop in 5-12m.
incident-bot: metric update 1m after mitigation -> 5xx rate down to 9%, queue_length=180, p95=750ms
maya cox: good signal. continuing to monitor. routing -> shared handled ~22% as expected.
ryan kim: keep watch for OOMs once new nodes come online; double-check model kernel flags (quantized path) to avoid hot OOM.
ops-runner: new nodes joined, model warm-start success: models loaded on node-9,node-10.
incident-bot: metric update -> 5xx rate 4%, p95 420ms, queue_length=60
maya cox: error rate approaching normal. lifting non-prod rate-limits, keeping overflow at 10% for gradual rollback.
novus-cs: Novus confirmed saw drop in errors and restored traffic. they want a post-incident writeup.
sre-lead: root cause hypothesis: KV cache evictions + a burst of long-sequence requests from Novus caused worker memory pressure and OOM churn, leading to queue buildup and latency. reserved pool sizing too tight for burst profile.
ryan kim: follow-ups: 1) add tenant-specific tail throttling rule when queue > 200, 2) add predictive autoscale rule based on 95th latency + kv-evict events, 3) review model quantization flags for Novus model.
maya cox: I'll open follow-up tickets and schedule a handoff doc for the week shift.
ops-runner: leaving a runbook note in infra-runbooks: "Novus reserved-pool saturation — steps taken: overflow routing, temp rate-limit, add nodes".
incident-bot: Incident resolved -- paging closed by maya cox :white_check_mark:
maya cox: handing off to night oncall @ryan kim. leaving notes: monitor p95 for 2h, keep overflow at 10% until follow-ups done.
ryan kim: ack. I'll own the follow-ups in the oncall board. thanks team. :thumbsup:
novus-cs: thanks everyone, relaying to customer.
